Campaign brief: The reader can make a better membership decision by comparing the documented benefits, price and eligibility conditions with the visits they realistically expect to make.
events.reader:
Selected audience: A couple aged 26 or over at the same address who expect to visit historic places, gardens or countryside together.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (vendor_claim; check applicability): They are considering one shared membership covering two adults rather than arranging and paying for visits separately. Joint membership costs £168 a year or £14 a month and requires both adults to be aged 26 or over and live at the same address.
User-specified audience: UK adults considering membership for historic places and outdoor visits
events.reader_segment: A couple aged 26 or over at the same address who expect to visit historic places, gardens or countryside together
events.promise: The reader can make a better membership decision by comparing the documented benefits, price and eligibility conditions with the visits they realistically expect to make.
events.arc: Move from uncertainty about likely use to a practical fit check: establish what joint membership covers, identify the benefits relevant to planned visits, then invite the reader to review all options and conditions before deciding.

emails.job: Help the reader compare joint membership with their own planned visits and decide whether to explore the available membership options further.
emails.single_idea: Joint membership may suit two eligible adults planning visits together, but its fit should be judged against the visits they actually expect to make rather than an assumed saving.
emails.objection: We may not visit often enough for membership to justify the annual price.
must_not_say: That membership will save the reader money or pay for itself.
A visit-frequency break-even point or comparison with individual admission prices.
That parking is free at every National Trust car park.
That every place, historic property or outdoor space is included or always open.
Local places, opening hours, events or discounts.
That monthly payments reduce the annual price or remove the commitment.
Guest-pass, family, junior, young-person, lifetime, senior, gift, Explorer Pass, accessibility or renewal details; these would dilute the single fit-check argument.
Any new-launch language, urgency, guarantee, testimonial or popularity claim.
emails.felt_need: We are considering several days out together, but we are not sure whether membership would suit how often and where we plan to visit.
emails.status_quo: They can continue considering visits individually or compare their plans with the published membership terms; the evidence does not establish how they currently pay for days out.
emails.mechanism: Joint membership covers two adults aged 26 or over living at the same address for £168 a year or 12 monthly payments of £14. Membership includes free entry to more than 500 places in the National Trust's care and free parking at most National Trust car parks, giving the reader concrete terms to compare with their intended visits.
emails.call_to_action: Review the membership options and conditions at https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/membership
emails.next_step_decision: Decide which membership option, if any, matches the reader's household, eligibility and planned visits.
emails.next_step_value: The official membership page lets the reader review membership types, prices, eligibility conditions and stated visitor benefits.
emails.next_step_limit: Reviewing the page cannot determine how often this household will visit, guarantee savings, confirm parking at every intended location or establish a personal break-even point.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Membership can be considered not only for its visitor benefits but also as a way to support the care of houses, gardens, coastlines and countryside.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: We want our days out to support places we value, but that still needs to sit alongside a membership arrangement that suits us.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Membership revenue goes towards looking after nature, beauty and history, while member support helps care for hundreds of places including houses, gardens, coastlines and countryside.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: views membership only as a calculation about visits. After: sees that supporting the care of places is another documented reason to consider it, while recognising that personal fit still depends on the published options and conditions.
must_not_say: That membership produces a measurable conservation result for each member.
That supporting the National Trust makes membership financially worthwhile.
Customer stories, popularity claims or attributed outcomes.
Any guarantee about access, savings or the future condition of places.
alternative_arguments.objection: I would rather pay only when I visit or support conservation another way than commit to membership.
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Review the membership options and conditions at https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/membership
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the combination of supporting places and receiving membership benefits is relevant enough to compare the available plans.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The official membership page explains what member support contributes towards and presents the membership offer for further review.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page does not establish whether membership is better for this reader than paying per visit or donating directly.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame membership as helping care for the kinds of places the reader wants to visit, without sentimentality or implying a measurable personal impact.
